description: Stereo send and return hub: three effect paths, and three stages that each choose one path, send the signal out to it and crossfade its return back in, either down a chain or side by side

params.text: Switches that stage in and out of circuit, fading over the time set by FADE; out of circuit the signal passes to the next stage untouched. It reads 1 when the stage is in, despite the name Bypass
Steps that stage through the three effect paths, A then B then C; it lights in the colour of the path chosen — cyan, magenta or orange — and brightens with that stage's mix knob
Sets how much of that stage's return is crossfaded against the signal arriving at that stage; at zero nothing is sent out at all, and any setting above zero sends at full strength
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting how far that stage's mix CV input moves its mix knob
Chooses between running the stages as a chain in the order I, II, III and feeding each one a copy of the main input to be summed; the tooltip calls these Sequential, the default, and Parallel
A press exchanges the effect paths chosen by stages I and II, dropping both to near silence for about 10ms and fading them back over the time set by FADE
A press exchanges the effect paths chosen by stages II and III, dropping both to near silence for about 10ms and fading them back over the time set by FADE
A press exchanges the effect paths chosen by stages III and I, dropping both to near silence for about 10ms and fading them back over the time set by FADE
Sets the fade time shared by all three stages when one is bypassed or swapped; zero makes the change instant, and the maximum of 3 gives a fade of a few seconds
Crossfades the main outputs between the dry main input and what the stages return; it comes up fully wet, so the dry input is heard only through the stages

inputs.text: Takes the right side back from that path's effect; with no cable in it the left return of the same path feeds both sides
Takes the left side back from that path's effect; how much of it reaches the output is set by the mix knob of whichever stage has chosen this path
The left side of the signal the module works on; a polyphonic cable here has its channels averaged into one
The right side of the signal the module works on; with no cable in it the left input feeds both sides
Moves that stage's mix, scaled by that stage's attenuverter and added to its mix knob; 0-10V covers the whole range at a full attenuverter, and the total is clamped between 0 and 1
A pulse here toggles that stage in and out of circuit. Held for more than 1000 samples it acts as a gate instead: the stage is in circuit while the gate is high and out when it falls
A rising edge above 2V exchanges the effect paths chosen by stages I and II
A rising edge above 2V exchanges the effect paths chosen by stages II and III
A rising edge above 2V exchanges the effect paths chosen by stages III and I

outputs.text: Feeds that path's effect with the left side of the signal. Sending stops when the stage using the path is bypassed or its mix is zero; in the parallel mode the main input goes out here regardless
Feeds that path's effect with the right side of the signal. Sending stops when the stage using the path is bypassed or its mix is zero; in the parallel mode the main input goes out here regardless
The left side of the finished signal: what the stages return, crossfaded against the dry main input by MIX
The right side of the finished signal: what the stages return, crossfaded against the dry main input by MIX

notes: In the chain mode the signal runs through the stages in the order I, II, III; in the parallel mode each stage takes a copy of the main input and the three returns are summed
In the parallel mode the main outputs carry only the summed returns, so with MIX fully wet and no return patched they read 0V; in the chain mode an unpatched path passes the signal on
The parallel mode makes the module a three-channel stereo mixer on its own: patch three sources into the return inputs and leave the main input and the sends unpatched
Two stages set to the same path build a feedback loop through the effect patched there; bypassing either stage or turning either stage's mix knob to zero cuts the loop
Wherever the module takes a stereo pair, the left jack feeds both sides when the right one has no cable in it
A polyphonic cable into the left or right input has its channels averaged into one, and every output of the module carries a single channel
Bypassing a stage fades it out or in over the time set by FADE; a swap drops both stages to near silence in about 10ms first, then fades them back over that same time
